comment: The guest speakers were fantastic!! Loved them. The regular lectures by contrast are two hours of one-way talking with zero discussion, which is hard to sit through.
summary: Loved the guest speakers but found regular two-hour lectures one-way with no discussion.

comment: Prof explains things really well and the examples are fun, but the semester feels like it ends in a sprint. Graph algorithms in the last two weeks was too much to absorb.
summary: Likes the explanations but felt the last two weeks on graph algorithms were a rushed sprint.

comment: Exams were fair and tested what was taught. Rubric on the lab reports was detailed so I always knew where marks came from.
summary: Found exams fair and the detailed lab report rubric clear about how marks were awarded.

comment: lectures were engaging, lots of demos and the clicker questions kept me awake at 9am
summary: Found lectures engaging, with demos and clicker questions keeping students alert at 9am.

comment: SolidWorks training was solid and i like that we get a student licence. But the submission portal rejects files over 10MB so my assembly never uploaded and I had to email it, then got marked late.
summary: Likes the SolidWorks training but the portal's 10MB upload limit blocked an assembly, which was then marked late.

comment: The pandas lab was brilliant, learned more in two hours than in weeks of reading. But the homework sets are just copy-pasting from the lab with different column names, so they feel like busywork.
summary: Praises the pandas lab but finds the homework repetitive busywork copied from lab patterns.

comment: Love the topic and the real datasets. The weekly problem sets alone are okay but with the quiz AND the discussion post AND the group memo all landing in the same week, it was too much.
summary: Enjoys the real datasets but struggled when quiz, discussion post and group memo all landed in the same week.

comment: This class is not 3 credits, it is a full time job. Between the weekly sprint reports, the peer reviews, the standups and the actual coding I was spending 20+ hours a week on this alone and my other courses suffered. Whoever planned the deliverables did not talk to the other instructors.
summary: Weekly sprint reports, peer reviews and coding took over 20 hours a week, hurting other courses.

comment: ok so my problem is the shape of the whole term. we spent like four weeks on nomenclature, which honestly I could have learned in one, everybody was bored and checking their phones, and then suddenly in the second half we had to do substitution AND elimination AND the first synthesis problems in about ten days. I was drowning by week 9 and the people who studied ahead were the only ones who survived. Very unbalanced pacing, please redistribute the time.
summary: Pacing is unbalanced: four slow weeks on nomenclature, then substitution and elimination reactions rushed in about ten days.

comment: Gradescope autograder with instant feedback is amazing, I could fix my code before the deadline.
summary: Loves Gradescope's instant autograder feedback, which allowed fixes before deadlines.

comment: The midterm had a whole question on a topic that was never mentioned in lecture or the homework. Then the curve was applied in a way no one understood and we got zero explanation of grades. Feels arbitrary.
summary: Midterm included an untaught topic, and the unexplained curve made grading feel arbitrary.

comment: lecture structure confusing, jumps between topics, no clear outline. sometime i dont know what we are learning today. also he talk very quiet in the back
summary: Lectures jump between topics without an outline, and the lecturer is too quiet to hear from the back.

comment: Moodle is a nightmare. Links break, the quiz timer froze on me, and the audio on the recorded lectures cuts out every few minutes. I'm paying a lot for this.
summary: Moodle has broken links and a frozen quiz timer, and recorded lecture audio cuts out repeatedly.

comment: the essays have nothing to do with what we discuss in class. prompt 2 was about a thinker we never covered. what is the point
summary: Essay prompts seem unrelated to class discussions; prompt 2 covered a thinker never taught.

comment: Readings are way too outdated. Some of the articles are from the 90s and the drug guidelines have changed since. Please refresh the reading list.
summary: Reading list is outdated, with 1990s articles that conflict with current drug guidelines.

comment: Surprisingly light workload for a studio course, i had time to actually iterate on my posters and still work my part time job
summary: Pleased the light workload left time to iterate on posters alongside a part-time job.

comment: Office hours with the TA were a lifesaver. She would work through my wrong approach instead of just giving the answer.
summary: Values the TA's office hours for guiding students through their mistakes rather than giving answers.

comment: The final project (building our own portfolio site) was the most useful thing I did all semester. Instructions were clear and it directly relates to job hunting.
summary: Found the portfolio-site final project clear, relevant and the most useful work of the semester.

comment: I came in worried about keeping up since I'd been away from school for ten years, but the way the first month built slowly from supply and demand up to the AD-AS model made it very manageable. Thank you for not skipping steps.
summary: Appreciates the gradual first-month build from supply and demand to AD-AS, which suited a returning student.

comment: The short documentary videos in weeks 2 and 5 were excellent and made the readings come alive.
summary: Praises the week 2 and 5 documentary videos for bringing the readings to life.

comment: I really like the course content and the demos. Honestly though the lectures start late every time, with 15 minutes of rambling stories before any chemistry, so the actual mechanism teaching gets squeezed.
summary: Likes the content but lectures open with long off-topic stories, squeezing the actual mechanism teaching.

comment: Perfect speed. Never felt rushed and never bored, which is rare for a coding class.
summary: Found the overall pace well balanced, neither rushed nor boring.

comment: Gradescope feedback on the compositions was really detailed, thank you!
summary: Thanks instructor for detailed Gradescope feedback on compositions.

comment: The Piazza forum is a ghost town. Questions sit there for days with zero instructor input and the TAs seem to have no idea about the project requirements.
summary: Forum questions sit unanswered for days and TAs seem unaware of project requirements.

comment: grading is soooo random. my friend wrote basically the same essay as me and got a B+ while I got a C. great fairness guys, 10/10
summary: Sarcastically criticises inconsistent essay grading, citing a near-identical essay scoring higher.

comment: I emailed three times about my missing grade in week 9 and got no response for over two weeks. By then it was too late to fix anything. Very disappointing.
summary: Emails about a missing week 9 grade went unanswered for over two weeks, too late to fix.

comment: Case study write ups are a good way to apply the material. Sadly the instructions never say how long they should be or how many sources, so everyone guessed and some of us lost points.
summary: Likes case study write-ups but instructions omit length and source requirements, leading to guesswork.

comment: Assignment 3 instructions were contradictory - the PDF said use UDP, the starter code was TCP, and the forum answers said either. I wasted a whole weekend. Please proofread before releasing.
summary: Assignment 3 instructions contradicted each other on UDP versus TCP, wasting a weekend.

comment: The lectures are just the professor reading the slides aloud in a monotone. I stopped attending after week 3 since I can read them myself faster. No examples, no questions, nothing.
summary: Lectures consist of reading slides in a monotone; stopped attending after week 3 as they add nothing.

comment: TA was knowledgeable in the lab sessions. Pity the main instructor only ever says 'check the syllabus' when you ask something, felt dismissed.
summary: Appreciates the knowledgeable lab TA but the main instructor dismisses questions by saying check the syllabus.

comment: Textbook explanations are really clear and the practice problems at the end of chapters are great, but the lecture slides on Canvas are just screenshots of the book with no added content, there's nothing to review from.
summary: Likes the clear textbook but says the slides are only book screenshots, offering nothing extra for revision.

comment: WEEK 7 WAS INSANE. series convergence tests, all five of them, in two lectures?? then a quiz on it friday. no.
summary: Week 7 series convergence tests were crammed into two lectures before a Friday quiz.

comment: Good seminar discussions, great reading list. However we got through the entire interwar period in one session and then spent three weeks on the Congress of Vienna. Reshuffle the time please.
summary: Values seminar discussions but felt the interwar period was rushed while the Congress of Vienna dragged for three weeks.

comment: Way too many deliverables. Please cut some.
summary: Asks the instructor to cut the excessive number of deliverables.

comment: good assignments, the field data one in week 6 was fun
summary: Enjoyed the assignments, especially the week 6 field data task.

comment: the lab machines in room B14 are so slow, Oracle takes like 10 min to open and crashed twice during the week 8 lab and lost my work. fix them
summary: Slow room B14 lab machines made Oracle take ten minutes and crashed twice in week 8, losing work.

comment: Heavy but fair. Clinical prep took about 8 hours a week and it was always clear why.
summary: Considers the roughly eight weekly hours of clinical prep heavy but fair and purposeful.

comment: Professor is very kind and his office hours are always welcoming, but only one hour a week for 150 students is impossible, the queue was out the door and I never got to ask my question.
summary: Finds the professor welcoming but one weekly office hour for 150 students meant long queues and no chance to ask.

comment: The textbook is free online and actually well written, plus the lecture notes PDFs are neat. Saved me a lot of money.
summary: Appreciates the free, well-written online textbook and neat lecture note PDFs.

comment: The RStudio cloud setup meant I didn't have to install anything on my old laptop. Everything just worked from day one.
summary: Appreciates the RStudio cloud setup that worked immediately without any local installation.

comment: Cases are interesting and I learned a lot. The reading volume though, 80 pages per class, is unrealistic for someone with a job. I had to skim most of it.
summary: Finds cases interesting but 80 pages of reading per class is unrealistic alongside a job.

comment: Prof. M's lectures are the reason I'm switching to a math minor. Every proof was motivated before it was written down.
summary: Praises lectures that motivate each proof before presenting it, inspiring a math minor.

comment: prof replies to emails on weekends too?? unreal. thanks
summary: Impressed the professor answers emails even on weekends.

comment: slides are full of typos and some of the equations are wrong (slide 34 of lecture 6 for sure). the recommended textbook is also a different edition than what the course follows so page numbers dont match
summary: Slides contain typos and equation errors (lecture 6, slide 34), and textbook edition page numbers do not match.

comment: Zoom classes are generally fine. The sound is another story though, the instructor's microphone echoes and I constantly had to turn the volume up, then got blasted when students unmuted.
summary: Zoom sessions generally work well, but the instructor's echoing microphone makes audio hard to follow.

comment: The quizzes are a good way to keep up with readings. However the exam feedback was just a number, no comments at all, so I have no idea what I did wrong on the short answers.
summary: Likes the reading quizzes but received only a number on the exam with no feedback on short answers.

comment: Great selection of short stories to read, I discovered so many authors. I wish the handouts on craft weren't scanned crooked photocopies, half of the text is unreadable on my phone.
summary: Enjoys the short story selection but craft handouts are crooked scans that are hard to read on a phone.

comment: Lectures are great and the homework prepares you well. But the final was 40% of the grade and one bad day can ruin everything, would prefer more small quizzes.
summary: Appreciates the lectures and homework but dislikes the final being 40% of the grade; wants more small quizzes.
